rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest analysis takes ḥaythumā as conditional; the added mā is required for that force, contrary to al-Farrāʾ.
rows.anchor: في " حيثما " هنا وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها شرطية، وشرط كونها كذلك زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the conditional analysis, kuntum is jussive, wallū answers the condition, and ḥaythumā is an accusative adverb governed by kuntum; Q 17:110 illustrates the construction.
rows.anchor: ب " كنتم " ، في محل جزم بها، و " فولوا " جوابها وتكون هي منصوبة على الظرف بكنتم،

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Although ḥayth is a locative noun normally annexed to a clause in the genitive, its connection with mā removes annexation and gives it conditional force and verbal governance.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وحيث هي ظرف مكان مضافة إلى الجملة فهي مقتضية للخفض بعدها،

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ treats ḥayth as a nonconditional adverb governed by wallū; the author rejects this because added mā necessarily makes it conditional.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها ظرف غير مضمن معنى الشرط، والناصب له قوله: " فولوا " قاله أبو البقاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wallū derives from waliyū: the heavy ḍamma on yā is dropped, then yā is deleted at the meeting of two sukūns and the preceding vowel is rounded to match the pronoun.
rows.anchor: وأصل ولوا: وليوا، فاستثقلت الضمة على الياء فحذفت فالتقى ساكنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatrahu has two analyses: it is either the direct object or an adverb of direction, as discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وقوله: " شطره " فيه القولان، وهما: إما المفعول به وإما الظرفية

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: For the majority, the clause anna-hu al-ḥaqq supplies both objects of yaʿlamūn.
rows.anchor: قوله: { أنه الحق } يحتمل أن تكون " أن " واسمها وخبرها سادة مسد المفعولين ل " يعلمون " عند الجمهور،

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows the clause to supply one object of a verb taking two, with the second object omitted.
rows.anchor: ومسد أحدهما عند الأخفش والثاني محذوف على أنها تتعدى لاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis has the clause supply one object because yaʿlamūn means to recognize or know.
rows.anchor: وأن تكون سادة مسد مفعول واحد على أنها بمعنى العرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed antecedent of the pronoun in annahu is the turning toward the qibla implied by wallū.
rows.anchor: أحدها: يعود على التولي المدلول عليه بقوله: " فولوا ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second proposed antecedent of the pronoun in annahu is the direction, shatrahu.
rows.anchor: والثاني: على الشطر. والثالث: على النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view refers the pronoun to the Prophet; this shifts from direct address in fa-lanuwalliyannaka to speaking of him in the third person.
rows.anchor: والثالث: على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويكون على هذا التفاتا من خطابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min rabbihim modifies an omitted circumstantial expression describing al-ḥaqq: the truth is from their Lord.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من الحق أي: الحق كائنا من ربهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person reading may address the People of the Book or refer back to the believers, with a shift from the preceding address.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: " عما يعملون " بالغيبة ردا على الذين أوتوا الكتاب أو ردا على المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct-address reading most naturally addresses the believers; it may instead turn to the People of the Book to spur them on.
rows.anchor: وبالخطاب على رده للمؤمنين وهو الظاهر، أو للذين على الالتفات تحريكا لهم وتنشيطا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred parse makes alladhīna an accusative adjective qualifying al-ṣābirīn.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة }: فيه أربعة أوجه، أحدها: أن يكون منصوبا على النعت للصابرين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, alladhīna is accusative by way of praise.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون منصوبا على المدح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nominative parse supplies an omitted subject, hum alladhīna; it may be a cut-off construction or a fresh resumption.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون مرفوعا على خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي: هم الذين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhīna may instead be the subject, with the conditional clause as its relative clause and the following أولئك عليهم صلوات as its predicate.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أن يكون مبتدأ، والجملة الشرطية من " إذا " وجوابها صلته، وخبره ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A first parse makes ajību a nominative adjectival clause describing qarīb.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب }: في " أجيب " وجهان أحدهما:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ajību is a second predicate of innī, following qarīb as the first predicate.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنها خبر ثان لإني، لأن " قريب " خبر أول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implied command to speak follows the conditional fāʾ: say to them that God is near, since nearness is the condition's reported consequence.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من إضمار قول بعد فاء الجزاء تقديره: فقل لهم إني قريب، وإنما احتجنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajību follows the pronoun preceding the predicate rather than switching to third-person agreement with qarīb, the more usual Arab pattern; the author cites Q 27:55, Q 27:47, and an unattributed poem.
rows.anchor: وجاء قوله " أجيب " مراعاة للضمير السابق على الخبر، ولم يراع الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in ʿannī and innī moves from third-person reference to first-person speech; the preceding explicit name of God functions like a third-person pronoun.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: { عني } و " إني " التفات من غيبة إلى تكلم، لأن قبله، " ولتكبروا الله "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kaf addresses the Prophet even though he is not named here; the earlier phrase about revelation implies that the Quran was sent down to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: والكاف في " سألك " للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن لم يجر له ذكر، إلا أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearness is metaphorical for the speed of answering a caller, since God transcends bodily proximity and place; Q 50:16 and the cited report illustrate the wording.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: " فإني قريب " مجاز عن سرعة إجابته لدعوة داعيه، وإلا فهو متعال

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The second idhā may be a temporal adverb governed by ajību, meaning that He answers at the time of calling.
rows.anchor: والعامل في " إذا " قال الشيخ: " قوله: أجيب " يعني " إذا " الثانية

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The second idhā may instead be conditional, with its answer omitted as indicated by ajību, or ajību itself may be the answer under analyses allowing it before the condition.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن تكون لمجرد الظرفية وأن تكون شرطية، وحذف جوابها لدلالة " أجيب " عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first idhā is governed by the implied speech verb, fa-qul, in the reconstructed sentence.
rows.anchor: وأما " إذا " الأولى فإن العامل فيها ذلك القول المقدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in daʿwa marks the verbal noun's form, not a single occurrence; like raḥma and najda, it does not make the noun singular in event count.
rows.anchor: والهاء في " دعوة " ليست الدالة على المرة نحو: ضربة وقتلة، بل التي بني عليها المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two yāʾs are orthographic extra-letter variants absent from the codex form: readers omit them throughout, retain them in both positions, or retain them in connection but omit them at pause; the set has sixty-two yāʾs.
rows.anchor: والياءان من قوله: " الداع - دعان " من الزوائد عند القراء، ومعنى ذلك أن الصحابة لم تثبت

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وقالون
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn retain both yāʾs in connected reading and omit them at pause.
rows.anchor: فأثبت أبو عمرو وقالون هاتين الياءين وصلا وحذفاها وقفا.

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: One analysis keeps the request sense of the istifʿāl form: let them ask for My response.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه للطلب على بابه، والمعنى: فليطلبوا إجابتي قاله ثعلب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istajāba can function like ajāba, with istifʿāl matching ifʿāl; the author lists several other paired forms as parallels.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه بمعنى الإفعال، فيكون استفعل وأفعل بمعنى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Quran usage istajāba appears with a preposition; an unattributed poem uses it transitively, though the author allows that a preposition may have been omitted.
rows.anchor: ومن تعديه بنفسه قوله: 854 وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in fa-l-yastajībū is the imperative lām.
rows.anchor: واللام لام الأمر

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī says istajāba entails accepting the invitation, while ajāba is broader and can answer by opposing it; he cites Q 21:76 and Q 3:195.
rows.anchor: وفرق الرماني بين أجاب واستجاب: بأن " استجاب " لا يكون إلا فيما

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yarshudūn with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on shīn, from the past form rasha-da with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على " يرشدون " بفتح الياء وضم الشين، وماضيه رشد بالفتح

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla, with disagreement from one of them, read the shīn with kasra, from rashida with kasra in the past.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة بخلاف عنهما بكسر الشين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported reading puts fatḥa on the shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتحها. وماضيه رشد بالكسر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading of yarshudūn is also reported.
rows.anchor: وماضيه رشد بالكسر، وقرىء، يرشدون " مبنيا للمفعول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on shīn derives from arshada; its object is omitted, understood as guiding others.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: " يرشدون " بضم الياء وكسر الشين من أرشد. المفعول على هذا محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted complement of intahaw is عن القتال: if they desist, the condition means desist from fighting.
rows.anchor: ومتعلق الانتهاء محذوف؛ أي: عن القتال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intahaw is an iftaʿala form from nahā; its derivation from intahiyū involves deleting yāʾ after the heavy ḍamma, or changing yāʾ to alif after it moves and then deleting the alif at the meeting of two sukūns.
rows.anchor: وانتهى " افتعل " من النهي، وأصل انتهوا: انتهيوا، فاستثقلت الضمة على الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man may be a relative pronoun or an indefinite noun qualified by the following clause, as in a parallel earlier in the sūra.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { من يعجبك }: " من " يجوز أن تكون موصولة، وأن تكون نكرة موصوفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿjāb is finding something pleasing, inclining toward it, and esteeming it; the hamza makes the verb transitive.
rows.anchor: والإعجاب: استحسان الشيء والميل إليه والتعظيم له. والهمزة فيه للتعدي.

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines wonder as perplexity caused by ignorance of a thing's cause, relational rather than an intrinsic quality; a thing that amazes me appears in a way whose cause I do not know.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب: " العجب حيرة تعرض للإنسان

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unattributed poem uses ʿajibtu for wondering at a goat that insulted the speaker, though he had not struck it.
rows.anchor: ويقال: عجبت من كذا، قال: 893 عجبت والدهر كثير عجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī al-ḥayāt may modify qawlihi: he impresses the listener with claims about worldly affairs because he seeks worldly advantage through false professions of love.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يتعلق ب " قوله " ، أي: يعجبك ما يقوله في معنى الدنيا، لأن ادعاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fī al-ḥayāt modifies yuʿjibuka: his speech is pleasing and eloquent in worldly life, but not in the afterlife because of speech difficulty there or because he is not allowed to speak.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يتعلق ب " يعجبك " أي: قوله حلو فصيح في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh prefers attachment to yuʿjibuka, meaning the man speaks pleasing, polished words throughout his life and never switches to harsh speech; he rejects al-Zamakhsharī's construal.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " والذي يظهر أنه متعلق بيعجبك، لا على المعنى الذي قاله الزمخشري، بل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may coordinate with yuʿjibuka; it is then a relative clause without syntactic position, or an adjective in the nominative if man is indefinite.
rows.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها عطف على " يعجبك " ، فهي صلة لا محل لها من الإعراب أو صفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause is circumstantial, attached either to the concealed subject of yuʿjibuka or to the genitive pronoun in qawlihi; this restricts the admiration and speech unnaturally, and a positive imperfect seldom serves as a circumstantial clause without an implied huwa.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون حالية، وفي صاحبها حينئذ وجهان، أحدهما: أنه الضمير المرفوع المستكن

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yushhidu in the active, with ḍamma on the prefix and kasra on hāʾ, taking Allah as its object.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على ضم حرف المضارعة وكسر الهاء، مأخوذا من أشهد ونصب الجلالة مفعولا به.

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن محيصن
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Muḥayṣin read with fatḥa on both letters, making Allah the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن محيصن بفتحهما ورفع الجلالة فاعلا

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads yastashhidu Allāh; istifʿāl can mean ifʿāl and match the majority reading, or it can mean the bare verb شهد with Allah as object after an omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة أبي فيحتمل استفعل وجهين، أحدهما: أن يكون بمعنى أفعل

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority explanation takes the phrase as swearing by God and calling Him witness that the speaker is truthful; the author says the actual sense is that God knows the concealed contents of his heart.
rows.anchor: يحلف بالله ويشهده إنه صادق، وقد جاءت الشهادة بمعنى القسم

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects taking quadriliteral ashhada as an oath verb: oath usage belongs to triliteral shahida, so the mainstream reading means that God sees what is hidden in the man's heart.
rows.anchor: لأن المستعمل بمعنى القسم " شهد " الثلاثي لا " أشهد " الرباعي،

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To make the reported oath interpretation fit, an omitted phrase must say that he swears against his heart: what he privately holds is disbelief, so he swears to its opposite, the pleasing claim he presents.
rows.anchor: تقديره: ويحلف بالله على خلاف ما في قلبه، لأن الذي في قلبه هو الكفر،

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa's reading supports the sense that God sees the disbelief concealed in the man's heart.
rows.anchor: ويقوي هذا التأويل قراءة أبي حيوة؛ إذ معناها: ويطلع الله على ما في قلبه من الكفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax of wa-huwa aladdu al-khiṣām follows the alternatives given for the preceding clause, and it may additionally be circumstantial from the pronoun in yushhidu.
rows.anchor: الكلام في هذه الجملة كالتي قبلها، ونزيد عليها وجها آخر وهو أن تكون حالا من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-add means fiercely contentious, from lidad, intense disputation; an unattributed poem uses alad for a fierce opponent.
rows.anchor: والألد: الشديد من اللدد وهو شدة الخصومة، قال: 895 إن تحت التراب عزما وحزما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives lidad verb patterns for prevailing in disputation; an unattributed line uses talid for outdoing stubborn opponents.
rows.anchor: ويقال: لددت بكسر العين ألد بفتحها، ولددته بفتح العين ألد بضمها أي: غلبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man may be called alad, alandad, or yalandad; the feminine is ladda and the plural is lud, like ḥumur.
rows.anchor: ورجل ألد وألندد ويلندد، وامرأة لداء، والجمع لد كحمر.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives alad from the two lidadī of the neck, its sides.
rows.anchor: وفي اشتقاقه أقوال، أحدها: من لديدي العنق وهما صفحتاه قاله الزجاج،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation is from the two sides of a valley, also called lidadī because they curve.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من لديدي الوادي وهما جانباه، سميا بذلك لاعوجاجهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third derivation connects the word with ladda, to confine: the disputant holds his opponent back from conducting the argument.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من لده إذا حبسه فكأنه يحبس خصمه عن مفاوضته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse treats al-khiṣām as the plural of khaṣm, like kaʿb/kiʿāb, so no adjustment is needed for the predicate.
rows.anchor: وفي " الخصام " قولان، أحدهما: أنه جمع خصم/ بالفتح نحو: كعب وكعاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-khiṣām is a verbal noun, the predicate needs an interpretation: omit a first complement (his quarrel is the fiercest), a second complement (fiercest among disputants), or use the verbal noun as an agent adjective.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه مصدر، يقال: خاصم خصاما نحو: قاتل قتالا، وعلى هذا فلا بد من مصحح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal takes afʿal as noncomparative, meaning ladhīd al-khiṣām, and analyzes the phrase as an adjective annexed to its complement.
rows.anchor: ليست للتفضيل، بل هي بمعنى لديد الخصام، فهو من باب إضافة الصفة المشبهة.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says al-khiṣām means disputation and the annexation of al-add has the sense of fī, like thabata al-ghadr.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " والخصام المخاصمة، وإضافة الألد بمعنى " في " كقولهم:

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh rejects al-Zamakhsharī's fī-genitive analysis as contrary to the usual rule that afʿal is annexed to something of which it is a part, and notes that annexation meaning fī is weak.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا مخالف لما يزعمه النحاة من أن أفعل لا تضاف إلا إلى ما هي بعضه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposal takes huwa not as the pronoun of man, but as referring to the quarrel: his quarrel is the fiercest quarrel.
rows.anchor: وقيل: " هو " ليس ضمير " من " بل ضمير الخصومة يفسره سياق الكلام،

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ takes huwa as referring to the verbal source qawlihi, which is construed as khuṣām.
rows.anchor: وجعل أبو البقاء " هو " ضمير المصدر الذي هو " قوله " فإنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause may coordinate with yuʿjibuka, making it part of man’s relative or adjectival clause, or may begin a fresh report after the sentence about aladdu al-khiṣām.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة الشرطية تحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن تكون عطفا على ما قبلها وهو " يعجبك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken literally, tawallā and saʿā mean that he turns away physically and walks with his feet.
rows.anchor: والتولي والسعي يحتملان الحقيقة أي: تولى ببدنه عنك وسعى بقدميه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken metaphorically, tawallā is turning back from his earlier words and saʿā is work and earning; the author cites Q 53:39 and poems by Imruʾ al-Qays and an unnamed poet.
rows.anchor: والمجاز بأن يريد بالتولي الرجوع عن القول الأول، وبالسعي العمل والكسب من السعاية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿāya may also mean harmful speech that divides friends; an unattributed poem describes tale-bearers moving between companions like an enemy.
rows.anchor: والسعاية بالقول ما يقتضي التفريق بين الأخلاء، قال: 899 ما قلت ما قال وشاة سعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī al-arḍ modifies saʿā; though one might think walking is necessarily on earth, the phrase generalizes the scope: wherever he settles, he corrupts, so a general setting implies general corruption.
rows.anchor: قوله: { في الأرض } " متعلق ب " سعى " ، فإن قيل: معلوم أن السعي لا يكون إلا في الأرض قيل: لأنه يفيد العموم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose lām in li-yufsida attaches to saʿā and explains its aim.
rows.anchor: و " ليفسد " متعلق ب " سعى " علة له.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yuhliku as active causative from ahlaka, with al-ḥarth as object and the verb coordinated with li-yufsida; فساد already entails destruction, so crops and offspring are singled out, as in Q 2:98.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على: " يهلك " بضم الياء وكسر اللام ونصب الكاف. " الحرث " مفعول به،

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads wa-li-yuhlika with an explicit purpose lām, which has the same sense as the majority reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي: " وليهلك " بإظهار لام العلة وهي معنى قراءة الجمهور،

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, also reported from Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, reads yahliku from intransitive halaka, with al-ḥarth as subject and al-nasl coordinated to it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة - ورويت عن ابن كثير وأبي عمرو - " ويهلك الحرث والنسل " بفتح الياء وكسر اللام

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A group reads the causative yuhliku with the verb in the indicative; it may coordinate with yuʿjibuka, with saʿā as a future sense, an implied huwa, or a fresh sentence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قوم: " ويهلك الحرث " من أهلك، و " الحرث " مفعول به إلا أنهم رفعوا الكاف. وخرجت على أربعة أوجه:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb passively and raises al-ḥarth as its deputy subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " ويهلك " مبنيا للمفعول، " الحرث " رفعا،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also reads yahliku with fatḥa on yāʾ and lām and an indicative ending, making al-ḥarth the subject; the open imperfect vowel is rare because neither radical is guttural, as in rakana/yarkan.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أيضا: " ويهلك " بفتح الياء واللام ورفع الكاف، " الحرث " رفعا على الفاعلية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nasl is the verbal noun of nasala, to come out quickly, as camel hair or a bird's feathers shed; another view stresses successive emergence. Imruʾ al-Qays's tan-salu witnesses the sense, and Q 21:96 may fit either.
rows.anchor: والنسل: مصدر نسل ينسل أي: خرج بسرعة، ومنه: نسل وبر البعير، ونسل ريش الطائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥarth and al-nasl are verbal nouns by origin but function here as direct objects.
rows.anchor: و " الحرث والنسل " وإن كانا في الأصل مصدرين فإنهما هنا واقعان موقع المفعول به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause may be a fresh statement or coordinate with yuʿjibuka; the comparable passive in Q 2:11 raises the question of what serves as its deputy subject, a matter of scholarly disagreement.
rows.anchor: هذه الجملة الشرطية تحتمل الوجهين المتقدمين في نظيرتها، أعني كونها مستأنفة أو معطوفة على " يعجبك "

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the bāʾ as causative: pride compelled him to sin and made him commit it.
rows.anchor: قوله: " بالإثم " في هذه الباء ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أن تكون للتعدية وهو قول الزمخشري

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh objects that causative bāʾ normally follows an intransitive verb, as in Q 2:17 and 2:20; use with a transitive verb is rare, as in ṣakaktu al-ḥajara bi-l-ḥajar.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وباء التعدية بابها الفعل اللازم نحو: ذهب الله بنورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may mark cause: his sin caused pride to seize him; an unattributed poem says ignorance's pride took hold of someone.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أن تكون للسببية بمعنى أن إثمه كان سببا لأخذ العزة له كما في قوله: 901 أخذته عزة من جهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may mark accompaniment and function as a circumstantial phrase, describing either the pride as tainted by sin or the man as taken while committing sin.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أن تكون للمصاحبة فتكون في محل نصب على الحال، وفيها حينئذ وجهان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase uses rhetorical completion: bi-l-ithm disambiguates al-ʿizza, which can be praiseworthy (Q 63:8; 5:54), so the reader does not mistake this pride for a virtue.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله " العزة بالإثم " التتميم وهو نوع من علم البديع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary parse makes ḥasbuhu the subject and jahannam its predicate: Hell is sufficient for him.
rows.anchor: قوله: { فحسبه جهنم } " حسبه " مبتدأ و " جهنم " خبره

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows jahannam to be the subject of ḥasb; if ḥasb is an active participle originating as a verbal noun, its agent fills the predicate's place, strengthened by the linking fāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقيل: " جهنم " فاعل ب " حسب " ، ثم اختلف القائل بذلك في " حسب "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account treats ḥasb as an indeclinable verb-like particle, either past ka-fa-hum or an imperative; the author rejects this because ḥasb inflects and takes prepositions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل " حسب " اسم فعل، والقائل بذلك اختلف: فقيل: اسم [فعل] ماض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasb requires annexation without becoming definite; as subject it may take an extra bāʾ, as predicate it does not, and it has no dual, plural, or feminine forms even when describing those nouns.
rows.anchor: وهو من الأسماء اللازمة للإضافة، ولا يتعرف بإضافته إلى معرفة، تقول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Jahannam is a foreign word arabized from Kahanām and therefore diptote for proper-name status and foreignness.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هي أعجمية وعربت، وأصلها كهنام، فمنعها من الصرف للعلمية والعجمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred account is Arabic: its nūn is extra, its pattern faʿnal, and it is linked to a deep well called rakiya Jahnām or to jahm, abhorrence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هي عربية الأصل، والقائلون بذلك اختلفوا في نونها: هل هي زائدة أم أصلية؟ فالصحيح أنها زائدة ووزنها " فعنل "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A competing Arabic analysis makes the nūn original and the pattern faʿlal like ʿadbas, on the claim that faʿnal does not occur in Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل نونها أصلية ووزنها فعلل كعدبس، قال: لأن " فعنلا " مفقود في كلامهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that faʿnal is unattested, citing ḍaghanṭ, safanj, hajnaf, and zūnak as examples of the pattern.
rows.anchor: لكن الصحيح إثبات هذا البناء، وجاءت منه ألفاظ، قالوا: " ضغنط " من الضغاطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited examples also support treating the nūn in zūnak as extra, rather than treating its wāw as a root letter; its declension restriction is then tied to femininity and proper-name status.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله يدل على أن النون زائدة في " زونك " وعلى هذا فامتناعها للتأنيث والعلمية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted specific object of blame is Jahannam; omission is apt because al-mihād falls at the verse ending.
rows.anchor: " ولبئس المهاد " المخصوص بالذم محذوف، أي: ولبئس المهاد جهنم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of blame is parsed as subject, with the praise/blame clause as its predicate; the author rejects alternatives that delete an entire unsupported sentence and leave the clause disconnected.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على " بئس " وخلاف الناس فيها. وحذف هذا المخصوص بذلك على أنه مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mihād may be the plural of mahd, bedding prepared for sleep.
rows.anchor: والمهاد فيه قولان، أحدهما: أنه جمع " مهد " وهو ما يوطأ للنوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-mihād is a singular name for a bed prepared for sleep.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه اسم مفرد، سمي به الفراش الموطأ للنوم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Hell their bed is derisive irony: it replaces the bedding they would lie on, as in an unattributed poem where painful blows serve as a greeting.
rows.anchor: وهذا من باب التهكم والاستهزاء، أي: جعلت جهنم لهم بدل مهاد يفترشونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muṭallaqātu is a subject with yatarabbaṣna as predicate; the sentence may be declarative in form but command divorced women to wait, or it may be literal description.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والمطلقات يتربصن }: مبتدأ وخبر، وهل هذه الجملة من باب الخبر الواقع موقع الأمر

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans say the wording is itself an imperative with an omitted imperative lām.
rows.anchor: وقال الكوفيون: إن لفظها أمر على تقدير لام الأمر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A literal declarative reading reconstructs ḥukm al-muṭallaqāti an yatarabbaṣna, omitting ḥukm and the maṣdar particle an; the author calls this very remote.
rows.anchor: ومن جعلها على بابها قدر: وحكم المطلقات أن يتربصن، فحذف " حكم " من الأول و " أن " المصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarabbaṣa takes a direct object because it means intazara, to wait for.
rows.anchor: و " تربص " يتعدى بنفسه لأنه بمعنى انتظر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent analysis omits the object of tarabbaṣa, understood as marriage or husbands, and treats three quruʾ as a temporal adverb.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن يكون مفعول التربص محذوفا وهو الظاهر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, three quruʾ itself is the direct object: they wait for three cycles to pass.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون المفعول هو نفس " ثلاثة قروء " أي ينتظرون مضي ثلاثة قروء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent attachment makes bi-anfusihinna modify yatarabbaṣna, with bāʾ marking cause, because of themselves; this construction requires an explicit detached self-reference rather than a bound pronoun.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله: { بأنفسهن } فيحتمل وجهين، أحدهما وهو الظاهر: أن يتعلق ب " يتربصن " ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, anfusihinna emphatically restates the attached subject nun, with an extra bāʾ allowed before nafs or ʿayn; on this parse the phrase has no syntactic governor.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون " بأنفسهن " تأكيدا للمضمر المرفوع المتصل وهو النون، والباء زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that ordinary emphasis would require a separate nominative pronoun first, but the extra bāʾ makes this emphasis adjunct-like; he cites ba- phrases and al-Akhfash's report qāmū anfusahum.
rows.anchor: لا يقال: لا جائز أن تكون تأكيدا للضمير؛ لأنه كان يجب أن تؤكد بضمير رفع منفصل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis requires the women themselves to observe the waiting period, not have someone else observe it for them, heightening the intended force.
rows.anchor: وفائدة التوكيد هنا أن يباشرن التربص هن
